I think we should also (if we don't do it yet) auto-update formal-ai docket containter, if there is no running formal-ai tasks, also we can stop formal-ai container, if no formal-ai tasks are running. So formal-ai conteiner is started and connected to task's docket container via internal docker network only if tasks are running, yet the memory for formal-ai must be preserved between tasks and between restarts of the container for formal-ai. So if the container is stopped, and new version available we should update to latest version, and in such case we need to make sure Formal AI supports non destructive migrations between versions.

So in our hive-mind docker we only pin initial formal-ai version.

We also need to do the same to auto-update claude, codex, agent and other agentic CLIs (when no tasks are active and new version available). Or as each task are isolated in docker, we should support update inside each separate task's docker.

All missing features must be reported to all our upstream repositories.

Follow-up to the requested idle lifecycle and auto-update behavior in [this review comment](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2147#issuecomment-5228459541).

I confirmed the current gaps:

- `docker-compose.yml` starts the Formal AI service permanently (`restart: unless-stopped`) and makes the Hive Mind container depend on its health. It is not task-scoped today.
- Docker-isolated tasks receive the sidecar URL, but the sidecar is outside the task daemon/network. The requested task-only internal network is not implemented.
- Formal AI memory is persisted in a named volume, but replacing the image currently has no machine-readable memory-schema preflight, explicit migration transaction, or rollback contract. `/health` proves the binary is alive and reports its version; it does not prove persisted-memory compatibility.
- Claude, Codex, Agent, Gemini, Qwen, Copilot, and OpenCode are installed at Hive Mind image-build time. There is no idle-only runtime refresh mechanism today.

The responsibility split is:

- **Hive Mind:** count live tasks, pull only while idle, compare image digests, start/stop the sidecar on demand, create the internal network, attach only Formal AI task containers before releasing their startup gate, keep the named memory volume, orchestrate backup/rollback, and refresh the agentic CLI runtime only while no task is active.
- **Formal AI:** define whether an old persisted-memory schema is readable by a candidate binary and provide a non-destructive, atomic, idempotent migration/preflight contract that an unattended orchestrator can trust.

Upstream reports:

- **Blocking:** [formal-ai#982](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/982) — reproducible named-volume replacement case, current backup/pin workaround, proposed machine-readable preflight/transaction, and old-to-new/interruption/rollback acceptance tests.
- **Non-blocking:** [link-foundation/start#154](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/154) — native Docker `--network`/`--network-alias` support. Hive Mind can safely work around this one with `docker network connect` while its existing task startup gate is closed.

Per issue #2146's explicit instruction to report missing Formal AI features as blockers and pause the pull request until they are resolved, PR #2147 remains **draft**. I am not enabling a health-check-only `latest` replacement path: it could appear successful while silently damaging memory or making rollback impossible. The general agentic-CLI updater remains part of the Hive Mind follow-up scope; no upstream Agent defect is required merely to install its latest published package while Hive Mind is idle.

Evidence handoff is pushed in commit [`41345e91`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/commit/41345e91dfae0be3f81e745ac4fea5ebf0788dc2). Fresh final-head [CI run 31282238674](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/31282238674) passed (documentation validation plus formatting, ESLint, and duplication checks; code test jobs were correctly skipped for this evidence-only commit). The complete post-review analysis and 34,667-line solution log are now preserved in the case study. PR #2147 remains draft pending blocking [formal-ai#982](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/982); [start-command#154](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/154) remains non-blocking because the closed startup gate permits a safe `docker network connect` workaround.

Answering the last review comment point by point.

## Newer upstream versions — all consumed at their newest published release

| Upstream                                                 | Newest release          | Used here                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [formal-ai](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai) | v0.337.0                | `FORMAL_AI_BOOTSTRAP_VERSION = 0.337.0` (the **initial** image pin, as requested); `FORMAL_AI_MINIMUM_VERSION = 0.336.0` is the enforced runtime floor, because 0.336.0 is the release that shipped the persisted-memory upgrade contract the idle updater depends on |
| [agent](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent)         | js-0.25.8               | `MIN_AGENT_FORMAL_AI_VERSION = 0.25.8` — a Formal AI task refuses to start on anything older, because older releases answer with their _default_ model when they cannot parse `--model`                                                                             |
| [start](https://github.com/link-foundation/start)        | js-0.31.0 / rust-0.19.0 | the named-network support from #154 is what the sidecar attaches to. `rust-0.19.0` (published 45 minutes before this comment) also closes #156, but the matching **js-0.32.0 was never published** — see below. This repository installs the npm package, so the pin stays at the newest published `0.31.0`                                                                                                                                                                                     |

## What was missing after those releases — six upstream reports

Verifying the delivered releases against what this PR actually leans on, reading the first full CI run this branch ever got, and re-checking upstream releases once more before marking this ready, turned up six real gaps. Each is filed with a reproduction, the current downstream workaround, a concrete code-level fix and acceptance tests:

- **[link-assistant/agent#295](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/295)** — _Expose model routing as a stable machine-readable event, not as an English log message._ The provider-drift guard has to discriminate on the free-text `message: 'using explicit provider/model'` emitted at `js/src/cli/model-config.js:118`. Rewording that string is an ordinary non-breaking change upstream, but it would silently disable a downstream **safety** check. The report asks for an additive `model_resolved` event carrying `requested` / `providerID` / `modelID` / `source` / `matchesRequest`.
- **[link-foundation/start#156](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/156)** — _Docker isolation: allow attaching additional networks (`--network` should be repeatable)._ `docker run --network` **replaces** the default bridge, and `js/src/lib/docker-network-options.js` keeps only one value, so no single-network invocation can express "reach GitHub **and** the private sidecar". This was an acceptance item of #154 that did not ship in #155. **It shipped today**: [PR #157](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/pull/157) merged at 10:43 UTC and closed it.
- **[link-foundation/start#160](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/160)** — _…but the JavaScript release of #156 is blocked, and this is why._ [`JavaScript CI/CD` run 31380353470](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/actions/runs/31380353470) on `main` failed right after #157 merged, so the `Release` job was skipped: `js-v0.32.0` does not exist and `npm view start-command version` still answers `0.31.0`. The failing assertion prints only `'1' !== '0'`, so I reproduced the scenario locally — internal network, aliased sidecar, `docker create` on the bridge, `docker network connect`, `docker start`:

  ```
  PING formal-ai (172.19.0.2): 56 data bytes
  64 bytes from 172.19.0.2: seq=0 ttl=64 time=0.488 ms
  1 packets transmitted, 1 packets received, 0% packet loss
  wget: server returned error: HTTP/1.1 403 rate limit exceeded
  ```

  The feature is fine — the private alias resolves and the default route survives. The test probes egress with `https://api.github.com`, which rate limits unauthenticated callers per source IP; shared Actions runners hit `403`, and BusyBox `wget --spider` reports any status ≥ 400 as failure. Swapping the probe for `https://example.com` makes the same reproduction exit `0`. Filed with that reproduction and the one-line fix.
- **[link-assistant/formal-ai#988](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/988)** — _`cargo install formal-ai --locked` fails on a stock Rust image since 0.333.0._ The dependency tree now reaches `native-tls` → `openssl-sys`, which needs `pkg-config` and the OpenSSL headers at build time. `0.317.0` (what `main` pins) installs on the same image; 0.333.2, 0.336.0 and 0.337.0 do not. Nothing in the crate's own manifest changed, so the requirement is invisible from the release notes.
- **[link-assistant/web-capture#151](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/151)** and **[link-foundation/browser-commander#77](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/77)** — the two root causes of #988, one line each: `reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = [...] }` with `default-features` left at `true` (→ `default-tls` → `native-tls`), and `fantoccini = "0.21"` with default features (`default = ["native-tls"]` → `openssl`). Both paths have to be fixed for `openssl-sys` to leave the tree.

None of them blocks this PR — each has a working answer here — so, per the pause rule, development is not paused on them. The exact bodies of all ten documents this incident published are archived verbatim under [`docs/case-studies/issue-2146/data/upstream-issues/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/tree/issue-2146-9f3a1aa2efb9/docs/case-studies/issue-2146/data/upstream-issues) and indexed in the manifest.

## CI — two real failures found and fixed, not waited out

1. **`Check for Changesets` was red on every push.** The branch carried two changesets and `scripts/validate-changeset.mjs` requires exactly one per PR. Because `test-suites`, `test-compilation`, `test-execution`, `memory-check-linux` and `docker-pr-check` all gate on `!contains(needs.*.result, 'failure')`, that single failure silently skipped every heavy job — this branch's 44 changed files had never actually been built or tested by CI. Fixed by combining the two into one `minor` changeset.

2. **`docker-pr-check` then failed for real** (run 31378794502), in the Formal AI builder stage:

   ```
   error: failed to run custom build command for `openssl-sys v0.9.117`
     Could not find openssl via pkg-config: The pkg-config command could not be found.
     Make sure you also have the development packages of openssl installed.
   error: failed to compile `formal-ai v0.337.0`
   ```

   That is upstream #988 above, arriving through this PR's bump of `FORMAL_AI_VERSION` from 0.317.0 to 0.337.0. The four builder stages (`Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.dind`, `Dockerfile.formal-ai`, `coolify/Dockerfile`) now install `pkg-config` and `libssl-dev` and set `OPENSSL_STATIC=1`, so the binary copied into the Ubuntu 24.04 runtime carries no OpenSSL soname dependency. Verified locally end to end ([`experiments/issue-2146/formal-ai-openssl-probe.Dockerfile`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2146-9f3a1aa2efb9/experiments/issue-2146/formal-ai-openssl-probe.Dockerfile) reproduces the break and the fix side by side):

   ```
   #7 [fixed 4/4] RUN ldd /usr/local/cargo/bin/formal-ai && formal-ai --version
   #7 1.509 	libgcc_s.so.1 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libgcc_s.so.1
   #7 1.509 	libm.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libm.so.6
   #7 1.509 	libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6
   #7 1.624 formal-ai 0.337.0
   ```

   A regression test in `tests/test-issue-2059-formal-ai-dispatch.mjs` now asserts all four builder stages carry the build dependencies, so this cannot silently regress into the Docker job again.

Locally: `npm test` (default suite, 382 files), `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check` and `npm run check:duplication` all clean.

## What is left

Nothing in the issue description or in either review comment is outstanding in this repository, and no requirement here is waiting on an upstream fix. The open items above have working downstream answers, not prerequisites. One of them is a plain wait rather than a workaround: when start publishes `js-0.32.0` — which #160 is what blocks — the `start-command` pin can move and the task container can join both networks at launch instead of through `docker network connect` inside the start gate. That is a simplification, not a missing capability; the sidecar behaves identically either way. The one thing that cannot be closed from here is the original behavioral complaint — Formal AI's agent mode produced a plan and no code in every reproduction — which is tracked on its own upstream coding-capability track ([formal-ai#848](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/848), [formal-ai#904](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/904)). What this repository can do about it — refuse to call it a success, refuse to retry it forever, and refuse to quietly finish the work on another model — it now does.

`npm view start-command version` answers `0.32.1` and formal-ai's latest release is `v0.339.1` — exactly the versions this PR now pins.

## Open follow-ups: three, none blocking

- https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/295 — model routing should be a typed event, not an English log string. Non-blocking: it is the third defensive layer; distinct argv atoms and the 0.25.8 floor stop the incident on their own, and the guard works against every released 0.25.8+ build.
- https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/151 — `reqwest` default features pull `native-tls`/`openssl-sys` into consumers. Non-blocking: the symptom is already fixed downstream in formal-ai 0.339.0; the builder stages keep `pkg-config`/`libssl-dev`/`OPENSSL_STATIC=1` as inert defense in depth in case a future release drags `openssl-sys` back in.
- https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/77 — the same root-cause class via `fantoccini` default features. Non-blocking for the same reason, covered by the same defense in depth.

## What the latest commit changed

- Bootstrap pin `FORMAL_AI_VERSION` moved 0.337.0 → **0.339.1** in `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.dind`, `Dockerfile.formal-ai`, `coolify/Dockerfile`, and `FORMAL_AI_BOOTSTRAP_VERSION`. Before moving it, the four memory-contract sources were compared between the v0.337.0 and v0.339.1 tarballs: `cli_memory.rs`, `server.rs`, `shared_memory.rs` are byte-identical (matching SHA-256), and `memory/upgrade.rs` only adds an explicit advisory-lock release — no field, refusal code, or schema bound changed.
- `start-command` pin moved 0.31.0 → **0.32.1**. The additive `docker network connect` inside the closed start gate is deliberately kept: the released 0.32.1 sources implement repeatable `--network` as the identical `docker create` → `docker network connect` → `docker start` sequence, and the in-repo attach stays fail-closed on any installed start-command version instead of silently collapsing to one network on a pre-0.32.0 parser.
